900100.title: The First Prototype
900100.description:
The ugly first version: prototyping basics. The first prototype is gloriously ugly: the boxes for characters, the text for art, the game reduced to its single question — is the core fun. The build's rule is the speed: the prototype should take days, not months, because the learning is the product.

The prototype's discipline is the one-question: every prototype tests exactly one thing — the jump, the loop, the choice.

The prototype's fate is the bin or the build: most prototypes die, and that's the job. The first prototype teaches the making; the making teaches the game.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The First Prototype

900101.title: The Core Loop Workshop
900101.description:
The thirty seconds that repeat: designing the loop. The core loop is the thirty seconds that repeat: the action, the reward, the upgrade, the harder action — the heartbeat of the game. The workshop's method is the loop diagram: draw the circle, name each beat, and check that every beat earns the next.

The loop's test is the hundred repetitions: play the loop a hundred times, and the fun must survive.

The loop's tuning is the reward schedule: the drip of upgrades that keeps the circle spinning. The core loop is the game; everything else is the decoration.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Core Loop Workshop

900102.title: The Paper Prototype
900102.description:
Scissors and index cards: the paper build. The paper prototype builds the game from scissors and index cards: the board is the table, the pieces are the tokens, the players are the AI. The build's virtue is the speed — the paper version plays tonight, and the flaws show by midnight.

The prototype's honesty is the human computer: the players enforce the rules, so the broken rules surface fast.

The paper's limit is the known: it tests systems, not feel. The paper prototype teaches the systems; the systems teach the game.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Paper Prototype

900103.title: The Playtest Circle
900103.description:
The players who teach: running playtests. The playtest circle is the players who teach: the regulars who play the broken builds and tell the truth. The running's method is the silent watch — the designer observes, never explains, and the confusion is the data.

The circle's rules are the kindness: the testers are volunteers, and the feedback is the gift.

The circle's harvest is the pattern: one confused player is an anecdote; five are a redesign. The playtest circle teaches the game; the game teaches the humility.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Playtest Circle

900104.title: The Vertical Slice
900104.description:
The whole game in miniature: the slice. The vertical slice is the whole game in miniature: one level with final art, final sound, final feel — the proof that the vision works. The slice's purpose is the decision: the slice greenlights the production or kills the project.

The slice's discipline is the narrow: one level, done completely, rather than ten levels sketched.

The slice's danger is the demo trap: the slice so polished the team thinks the game is done. The vertical slice proves the vision; the production builds the game.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Vertical Slice

900105.title: The Scope Knife
900105.description:
Cutting the game to save it: scoping discipline. The scope knife cuts the game to save it: the features fall, and the core survives. The discipline's method is the priority sort — the must, the should, the nice — and the knife takes the nice first.

The knife's courage is the darling-killing: the beloved feature that costs a month must go.

The knife's reward is the shipped: the small complete game beats the vast unfinished. The scope knife teaches the finishing; the finishing teaches the game.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Scope Knife

900106.title: The Juice Pass
900106.description:
The feel layer: adding the juice. The juice pass adds the feel layer: the screen shake, the particles, the sound that sells the hit. The pass's method is the moment list — every action gets its feedback, and the feedback gets its polish.

The juice's rule is the restraint: the feel serves the game, never the reverse.

The juice's test is the mute: turn off the juice and the game should still work — then turn it on and feel the difference. The juice pass teaches the polish; the polish teaches the love.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Juice Pass

900107.title: The Tutorial That Teaches
900107.description:
The invisible teacher: tutorial design. The tutorial that teaches is invisible: the player learns by playing, and never reads a manual. The design's method is the doing — the game teaches the jump by requiring the jump, in a safe place.

The tutorial's rule is the one-thing: teach one idea at a time, then combine.

The tutorial's test is the fresh player: the never-played must finish without help. The tutorial teaches the game; the game teaches the player.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Tutorial That Teaches

900108.title: The Launch Checklist
900108.description:
The ship list: launching the game. The launch checklist is the ship list: the builds, the stores, the press, the servers — every item checked before the button. The list's chapters are the technical (the build works everywhere), the commercial (the page converts), and the human (the team sleeps).

The checklist's discipline is the freeze: the feature freeze, weeks before, and the only changes are the fixes.

The checklist's wisdom is the day-one patch's shame: the launched game should need nothing. The launch checklist ships the game; the game ships the dream.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Launch Checklist

900109.title: The Game Dev's Oath
900109.description:
The capstone: the maker's promise. The game dev's oath is the capstone: the maker's promise to the player. The oath's clauses are the respect (the player's time is sacred), the honesty (the game is what it claims), and the care (the game is finished).

The oath's practice is the daily: every build measured against the promise.

The oath's reward is the trust: the player who trusts returns. The oath binds the maker; the game keeps the promise.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Game Dev's Oath

900110.title: The Deck-Builder's Engine
900110.description:
The deck as the game: deck-building analyzed. The deck-builder's engine is the deck as the game: the player builds the deck during play, and the deck is the strategy. The mechanic's core is the acquisition — the market row, the currency, the choice of what to add.

The engine's tension is the dilution: every added card thins the good draws, so the building is the pruning.

The engine's variants are the paths: the thin deck, the fat deck, the trash archetype. The deck-builder teaches the building; the building teaches the choice.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Deck-Builder's Engine

900111.title: The Worker Placement Puzzle
900111.description:
The spots are the game: worker placement analyzed. The worker placement puzzle makes the spots the game: the workers claim the action spaces, and the blocking is the strategy. The mechanic's core is the scarcity — the spaces are fewer than the wants.

The puzzle's tension is the order: the first worker takes the best spot, so the turn order is the game.

The puzzle's variants are the twists: the bump, the lockout, the shared worker. The worker placement teaches the planning; the planning teaches the patience.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Worker Placement Puzzle

900112.title: The Push-Your-Luck Die
900112.description:
Roll again? The luck press analyzed. The push-your-luck die asks the game's oldest question: roll again. The mechanic's core is the escalating risk — the pot grows, the bust looms, and the player decides.

The press's psychology is the ownership: the player chose the risk, so the bust is theirs.

The press's math is the edge: the wise press knows the odds, and presses anyway sometimes. The push-your-luck teaches the nerve; the nerve teaches the story.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Push-Your-Luck Die

900113.title: The Hidden Traitor
900113.description:
The friend who isn't: the traitor analyzed. The hidden traitor plants the friend who isn't: the mechanic's core is the paranoia — every action is read twice, once for the game and once for the tell.

The traitor's craft is the balance: the traitor must be able to win, and the loyal must be able to catch.

The traitor's table is the theater: the accusations are the game. The hidden traitor teaches the reading; the reading teaches the doubt.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Hidden Traitor

900114.title: The Engine Builder
900114.description:
The machine that makes the win: engine-building analyzed. The engine builder constructs the machine that makes the win: the cards combine, the combos compound, and the engine hums. The mechanic's core is the synergy — the pieces worth more together than apart.

The builder's arc is the ramp: the slow start, the humming middle, the explosive end.

The builder's risk is the solitaire: the engine so absorbing the opponents vanish. The engine builder teaches the combo; the combo teaches the hum.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Engine Builder

900115.title: The Area Control Map
900115.description:
The map is the argument: area control analyzed. The area control map makes the map the argument: the regions are the points, and the majority is the win. The mechanic's core is the contest — the region is never safe, and the borders breathe.

The map's craft is the geometry: the chokepoints, the rich centers, the poor edges.

The map's drama is the swing: the region flips, and the table gasps. The area control teaches the territory; the territory teaches the fight.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Area Control Map

900116.title: The Drafting Table
900116.description:
Pick and pass: the draft analyzed. The drafting table deals the pick-and-pass: the hand circulates, each player takes one and passes the rest. The mechanic's core is the signal — the passed cards tell the table's story.

The draft's skill is the reading: the drafter reads the signals and hates the draft accordingly.

The draft's fairness is the rotation: the packs even out, and the skill shows. The drafting table teaches the signal; the signal teaches the table.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Drafting Table

900117.title: The Legacy Envelope
900117.description:
The game that changes: legacy analyzed. The legacy envelope seals the game that changes: the envelopes open, the rules evolve, the board remembers. The mechanic's core is the permanence — the sticker placed is placed forever.

The legacy's power is the story: the campaign is the game, and the table writes it.

The legacy's cost is the once: the game plays its arc and ends. The legacy envelope teaches the commitment; the commitment teaches the epic.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Legacy Envelope

900118.title: The Cooperative Crisis
900118.description:
All against the game: cooperation analyzed. The cooperative crisis pits all against the game: the mechanic's core is the shared loss — the table wins together or falls together.

The crisis's engine is the escalation: the game fights back harder as the players advance.

The crisis's shadow is the quarterback: the one player who plays everyone's turn. The cooperative crisis teaches the together; the together teaches the trust.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Cooperative Crisis

900119.title: The Mechanic's Atlas
900119.description:
The capstone: mapping the mechanic space. The mechanic's atlas is the capstone: the map of the mechanic space — the engines, the puzzles, the presses, each in its territory. The atlas's method is the taxonomy: the families, the hybrids, the evolutions.

The atlas's use is the design: the designer consults the map and finds the uncharted.

The atlas's truth is the combination: the new mechanics are the old ones, combined. The atlas maps the known; the designer sails beyond.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Mechanic's Atlas
